title: Depth-first traversal of a graph
summary: Starting from the initial vertex, recursively descend along unvisited neighbors, backtrack to the previous vertex at dead ends, and continue exploring remaining branches.
context: The connected undirected graph contains vertices 0 through 6 and 6 undirected edges: 0—1, 0—3, 1—2, 2—5, 4—5, and 5—6. Traversal starts at vertex 0; in this example, neighbors are inspected in the order 1 then 3 at vertex 0, and 4 then 6 at vertex 5.
description: Solid gray lines represent original edges of the undirected graph; straight blue dashed lines represent recursive descent into unvisited neighbors, and curved orange dashed lines represent returning after a call finishes—neither adds new edges to the graph. Parenthesized numbers 1 through 14 in the overview denote the 7 descents and 7 returns (including entering and returning from the initial outer call), not vertex IDs.

The step sequence presents these 14 events in 11 steps: steps 1 through 8 correspond to events 1 through 8, step 9 combines events 9 through 11, step 10 corresponds to event 12, and step 11 combines events 13 and 14.
result: List res records only first visits, and backtracking appends no vertices. Changing the order in which neighbors are inspected changes the resulting depth-first sequence; even after every vertex has been visited, all remaining recursive calls must still return.

frames.title: Visit starting vertex 0
frames.explanation: In the step figures, res records vertices in first-visit order and visited deduplicates them; braces list set members without implying order. The initial call enters vertex 0 (event 1), records it in res and visited, and then inspects its neighbors in the order 1 then 3. Current recursion call path: 0; res = [0], visited = {0}; both neighbors 1 and 3 of 0 are unvisited.
frames.key_state: At starting vertex 0, call path 0; res = [0], visited = {0}.
frames.announcement: Visit starting vertex 0 and record it first in res = [0].

frames.title: Descend from 0 to 1
frames.explanation: Vertex 0 has unvisited neighbors 1 and 3; this example first recursively enters 1 (event 2), recording newly visited 1 in res and visited, while leaving neighbor 3 to be explored after 1's branch returns. Current recursion call path: 0→1; res = [0, 1], visited = {0, 1}.
frames.key_state: Descend from 0 to 1, call path 0→1; res = [0, 1].
frames.announcement: Descend from 0 to 1; result updates to [0, 1].

frames.title: Descend from 1 to 2
frames.explanation: At vertex 1, neighbor 0 is already in visited, so skip 0 and recursively enter unvisited neighbor 2 (event 3), recording 2 in res and visited. Current recursion call path: 0→1→2; res = [0, 1, 2], visited = {0, 1, 2}.
frames.key_state: Descend from 1 to 2, call path 0→1→2; res = [0, 1, 2].
frames.announcement: Descend from 1 to 2; result updates to [0, 1, 2].

frames.title: Descend from 2 to 5
frames.explanation: At vertex 2, neighbor 1 is already visited, so the call continues recursively into unvisited neighbor 5 (event 4), recording 5 in res and visited. Current recursion call path: 0→1→2→5; res = [0, 1, 2, 5], visited = {0, 1, 2, 5}; vertex 5 still has unvisited neighbors 4 and 6.
frames.key_state: Descend from 2 to 5, call path 0→1→2→5; res = [0, 1, 2, 5].
frames.announcement: Descend from 2 to 5; result updates to [0, 1, 2, 5].

frames.title: Descend from 5 to 4
frames.explanation: At vertex 5, neighbor 2 is already visited; between remaining unvisited neighbors 4 and 6, this example first recursively enters 4 (event 5), recording 4 in res and visited. Current recursion call path: 0→1→2→5→4; res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4], visited = {0, 1, 2, 4, 5}; vertices 3 and 6 remain unvisited.
frames.key_state: Descend from 5 to 4, call path 0→1→2→5→4; res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4].
frames.announcement: Descend from 5 to 4; result updates to [0, 1, 2, 5, 4].

frames.title: Return from 4 to 5
frames.explanation: Vertex 4's only neighbor 5 is already visited, so the call on 4 finishes and returns to 5 (event 6). Returning to already visited 5 does not append it to res again. Current recursion call path: 0→1→2→5; res stays [0, 1, 2, 5, 4], visited stays {0, 1, 2, 4, 5}; neighbor 6 of 5 and neighbor 3 of 0 remain unvisited.
frames.key_state: Backtrack from 4 to 5, call path 0→1→2→5; no new visit, res stays [0, 1, 2, 5, 4].
frames.announcement: Return from 4 to 5 without re-recording visited vertices; result is unchanged.

frames.title: Descend from 5 to 6
frames.explanation: Back at vertex 5, inspect its remaining unvisited neighbor 6, recursively enter 6 (event 7), and record 6 in res and visited. Current recursion call path: 0→1→2→5→6; res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6], visited = {0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6}; only vertex 3 in the entire graph remains unvisited.
frames.key_state: Descend from 5 to 6, call path 0→1→2→5→6; res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6].
frames.announcement: Descend from 5 to 6; result updates to [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6].

frames.title: Return from 6 to 5
frames.explanation: Vertex 6's only neighbor 5 is already visited, so the call on 6 finishes and returns to 5 (event 8) with no new visit. Current recursion call path: 0→1→2→5; res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6], visited = {0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6}; all neighbors 2, 4, and 6 of vertex 5 have now been processed.
frames.key_state: Backtrack from 6 to 5, call path 0→1→2→5; all neighbors of 5 are processed, res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6].
frames.announcement: Return from 6 to 5 with no new visit; result stays [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6].

frames.title: Return consecutively to starting vertex 0
frames.explanation: With all neighbors of 5, 2, and 1 inspected, calls backtrack consecutively along 5→2→1→0: event 9 returns from 5 to 2, event 10 returns from 2 to 1, and event 11 returns from 1 to 0. Current recursion call path: 0; res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6], visited = {0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6}; starting vertex 0 still has unvisited neighbor branch 3 to explore.
frames.key_state: Events 9 through 11: backtrack consecutively along 5→2→1→0 to starting vertex 0; res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6], and 0 still must explore branch 3.
frames.announcement: Events 9 through 11: return consecutively through 5, 2, and 1 to starting vertex 0 with result unchanged, ready to explore 0's remaining branch 3.

frames.title: Descend from 0 to 3
frames.explanation: Now that neighbor branch 1 of 0 has completely returned, enter unvisited neighbor 3 (event 12) and record 3 in res and visited. Current recursion call path: 0→3; res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3], visited = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}; all 7 vertices have been visited, with only the final call returns remaining.
frames.key_state: Event 12: descend from 0 to the last unvisited vertex 3, call path 0→3; res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3].
frames.announcement: Event 12: descend from 0 to 3, recording the final vertex for result [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3].

frames.title: Finish all recursive calls
frames.explanation: Vertex 3's sole neighbor 0 is already visited, so 3 first returns to 0 (event 13); now all neighbors of starting vertex 0 have also been processed, and the outermost initial call returns as well (event 14), completing the depth-first traversal. The call stack is now empty; final res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3], visited = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, and starting vertex 0 carries an orange return marker in the figure.
frames.key_state: Events 13 and 14: 3 returns to 0 and the initial call returns, ending all recursion; final res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3].
frames.announcement: Events 13 and 14: 3 returns to 0 and the outermost call finishes, completing depth-first traversal.

frames.title: Depth-first traversal overview
frames.explanation: After entering starting vertex 0, recursion descends sequentially through 1, 2, 5, and 4 (events 1 through 5); 4 returns to 5 (event 6), then the call at 5 visits 6, which returns to 5 (events 7 and 8). Next, calls return consecutively along 5→2→1→0 (events 9 through 11), branch into 0's remaining neighbor 3 (event 12), and finally return from 3 to 0 and finish the initial call (events 13 and 14). The complete first-visit sequence is [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3]; the table below lists the events by their figure numbers, with return events adding no new visits.
frames.key_state: Complete first-visit order is [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3], across 7 descent events and 7 return events; backtracking adds no results.
frames.announcement: Show an overview of all 14 descent and return events in depth-first traversal.
